A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Normal Space|normal space]] and $A$, $B$ disjoint [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed sets]].
Then there is a [[Definition:Continuous Mapping (Topology)|continuous]] $f: X \to \closedint 0 1$ with $f = 0$ on $A$ and $f = 1$ on $B$.

B_source.statement:
A space $X$ is normal {{iff}} for every closed $C$ and open $U \supseteq C$ there is an open $V$ with:
:$C \subseteq V \subseteq \overline V \subseteq U$

substitutions.a single interpolating open set: a family U_r indexed by dyadic rationals r in [0, 1]

derived.the nested family: level sets of a continuous function

object_map.reformulation: Build a dyadic family of nested open sets by repeated interpolation, and read off f as the first level containing x.

validity_conditions: The dyadic rationals are dense in [0, 1], which makes f continuous.
Each interpolation step uses the reformulation of normality.
proof_plan:
Let $U_1 = X \setminus B$, an open set containing $A$.
By the source result, choose open $U_0$ with $A \subseteq U_0 \subseteq \overline {U_0} \subseteq U_1$.

By [[Principle of Mathematical Induction|induction]] on the denominator, for each dyadic rational $r \in \closedint 0 1$ choose open $U_r$ with $\overline {U_r} \subseteq U_s$ whenever $r < s$.
Each new $U_{\paren {2 k + 1} / 2^{n + 1} }$ is inserted between two existing levels by the source result.

Define $\map f x = \inf \set {r: x \in U_r}$, with $\inf \O = 1$.
Then $f = 0$ on $A \subseteq U_0$, and $f = 1$ on $B$, which meets no $U_r$.
